A.explanation: Current $I$ and potential difference $V$ give power $P = IV$, but energy $E = Pt$ still needs the unknown time $t$.

B.explanation: Resistance $R$ and current $I$ give power $P = I^2R$, but energy $E = I^2Rt$ still needs the unknown time $t$.

C.explanation: Energy transferred is $E = QV$, so total charge $Q$ and potential difference $V$ give energy directly with no time needed.

D.explanation: Total charge $Q$ and resistance $R$ alone cannot give $E$ because $E = Q^2R/t$ still contains the unknown time $t$.

hints: Notice the stem says the current flows for an unknown time, so any formula that still contains time $t$ cannot be evaluated.
Recall how potential difference is defined in terms of energy and charge: $V = E/Q$.
Check which pair multiplies directly to energy in joules without needing $t$, and which pairs only give power in watts.
walkthrough: Identify the constraint: the time $t$ for which the current flows is unknown, so the calculation must not require $t$.
State the governing definition: potential difference is work done per unit charge, $V = E/Q$, where $E$ is energy dissipated and $Q$ is total charge passing.
Rearrange to isolate energy: $E = QV$. This uses only total charge in coulombs and potential difference in volts.
Test the other pairs: $P = IV$ and $P = I^2R$ give power, and converting power to energy needs $E = Pt = IVt = I^2Rt$, which needs the unknown $t$.
Therefore total charge and potential difference are sufficient on their own. This is option C.
